Compute the torsional response of a solid circular shaft using small-deformation, linear-elastic mechanics with the following specifications.

The shaft has a uniform solid circular cross-section with diameter d = 30 mm and total length L = 1200 mm.

The material is AISI 1020 steel with shear modulus G = 76923.1 MPa (approximately 76.9 GPa).

The shaft is a cantilever in torsion: the end at x = 0 is fully fixed (rotation theta = 0), and the end at x = L = 1200 mm is free (no torsional restraint).

Two concentrated torques are applied: T1 = +200000 N·mm at x = L = 1200 mm (free end) and T2 = -200000 N·mm at x = a = 400 mm. No distributed torques or other loads are present.

There is no transverse shear force, no bending moment, and no combined loading. The only stress state is pure torsional shear.

Compute the polar moment of inertia as J = pi * d^4 / 32 and the outer radius as c = d / 2.

Segment the shaft into two regions: Segment 1 from x = 0 to x = 400 mm, and Segment 2 from x = 400 mm to x = 1200 mm.

Produce the internal torque diagram by summing torques on one side of each cut section. The internal torque in Segment 1 (0 to 400 mm) equals the algebraic sum of T1 and T2. The internal torque in Segment 2 (400 to 1200 mm) equals T1.

Compute the maximum torsional shear stress in each segment using tau_max = T_internal * c / J, reporting a separate value for Segment 1 and Segment 2.

Compute the angle of twist at x = L by summing the twist contributions of each segment: theta_L = (T_segment1 * L_segment1) / (G * J) + (T_segment2 * L_segment2) / (G * J), with L_segment1 = 400 mm and L_segment2 = 800 mm. The fixed end at x = 0 has theta = 0.

Present all governing relations explicitly: J = pi * d^4 / 32, tau = T * c / J, theta = T * L / (G * J), and the equilibrium-based internal torque expressions for each segment.

State the sign convention clearly: positive torque and positive rotation follow the right-hand rule along the positive x-axis.

Report numerical results with units: internal torque in N·mm, shear stress in MPa, and angle of twist in radians.
